turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Filtering for the highest `target` values (≈1000–1190 MPa)** reveals a very consistent processing signature that dominates the top of the dataset:

| Variable | High‑strength pattern |
|---|---|
| NT | **930** (max) — all top samples |
| THT, THt, THQCr | **30 / 0 / 0** (through‑hardening off) |
| CT | **930** (max carburizing/austenitizing temp) |
| DT | **~850–895** (high diffusion temp) |
| Dt | 15–70 (broad, insensitive) |
| QmT | 60–140 (broad) |
| TT | **160–200** (low tempering temp → high strength) |
| Tt | **120** (max) |
| TCr | **0.5** |
| C | **0.17–0.23** (low, avoids embrittlement) |
| Si | 0.26–0.35 |
| Mn | 0.5–0.85 |
| Ni / Cr / Mo | hardenability elements elevated; Cr≈0.5–1.17, Mo≈0.15–0.21 |
| RedRatio | 240–860 (lower/moderate) |
| P, S, dA, dB, dC | low (clean steel) |

**Robustness reasoning:** Rather than sit on any single extreme peak (e.g., Cr=1.17 max, which cannot tolerate a +5% excursion within range), I place each variable near the *center of the densely‑populated high‑performance cluster*. The top‑target samples repeatedly appear with moderate Cr (~0.9–1.0), moderate Ni (~0.5–0.6), Mo≈0.17, low C, low TT and Tt=120 — all giving 1000+ MPa. This region is broad (many neighboring rows all score high), so ±5% perturbations of any variable land on other observed high‑strength points rather than collapsing.

I keep NT/CT/DT at their proven high plateau (small ±5% still stays high, plenty of supporting rows), TT low but not at the extreme edge, and compositions comfortably interior so a ±5% shift stays inside populated high‑strength space.

## Proposal

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=340, DT=880, Dt=40, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.75, P=0.012, S=0.015, Ni=0.6, Cr=0.9, Cu=0.1, Mo=0.17, RedRatio=600, dA=0.04, dB=0.005, dC=0.005
